doc.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Learn the music you don't like before judging it
summary: He says better music is usually music you don't like, so study it before criticizing.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: You know what I'm saying? Oh yeah.
For example, in your own case, what would you -­

Well, if you don't like something, the reason you don't like it is because you either don't understand it or there's something there that's an obstacle for you, you know? Because if you understand something then it's easy, isn't it? Okay? So, if you hear something and you don't like it, check it out first. Check everything out about it. Learn it. Then if you still don't like it, you've got a license to say you don't like it. Just like people -- The Bible isn't true, right? Have you ever read The Bible? No. I never read it, but it's -- man wrote it. I mean, well, do you know anything? Well, yeah. They say in The Bible that, that -- they don't know. So how can you criticize something if you don't know about it? See?
